test_title: SSC Selection Post 2025 (Matriculation Level) Official Paper (Held On: 24 Jul, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which key goal does the Swachh Bharat Mission focus on?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sanitation and hygiene**__.
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 

__ 
 
• **Swachh Bharat Mission (SBM)** was launched by **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** on **2nd October 2014**, marking the birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi. 
 
• The mission primarily aims to achieve universal access to **sanitation facilities** and eliminate open defecation in India by constructing individual household toilets, community toilets, and public toilets. 
 
• The campaign emphasizes **behavioral change** to promote hygiene practices, including handwashing and waste segregation at the household level. 
 
• It also focuses on creating awareness about the importance of sanitation and hygiene through **public outreach programs**, school campaigns, and media engagement. 
 
• The Swachh Bharat Mission consists of two sub-missions: **Swachh Bharat Mission (Urban)** and **Swachh Bharat Mission (Gramin)**, addressing urban and rural sanitation challenges respectively. 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 

__ 
 
• **Objective of Swachh Bharat Mission:** 
 
 
• The mission aims to achieve a **clean and open defecation-free India** by **2nd October 2019**, coinciding with the 150th birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi. 
 
• Promote the use of bio-toilets, solid waste management, and proper drainage systems to ensure better sanitation infrastructure. 
 
• Encourage active participation from **government bodies, private sectors, NGOs, and citizens** in maintaining cleanliness. 
 
 
 
• **Funding Mechanism:** 
 
 
• The Swachh Bharat Mission is funded through allocations from the **central government, state governments, and private partnerships**. 
 
• The **Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR)** contributions also play a significant role in funding sanitation-related projects. 
 
 
 
• **Achievements:** 
 
 
• As of **2023**, India has successfully constructed more than **11 crore toilets** under the Swachh Bharat Mission. 
 
• Over **600,000 villages** have been declared open defecation-free (ODF), contributing to improved public health and hygiene. 
 
 
 
• **Impact on Public Health:** 
 
 
• Reduction in diseases such as **diarrhea, cholera, and typhoid** due to improved sanitation facilities. 
 
• Enhanced quality of life in rural and urban areas through better waste management and hygiene practices. 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 

 
 
• **Key Features:** 
 
 
• **Urban Component:** Focuses on waste management, sewer networks, and public toilets in cities and towns. 
 
• **Rural Component:** Targets the construction of individual household latrines and awareness campaigns in villages. 
 
• **Behavioral Change:** Encourages citizens to adopt hygiene practices such as handwashing and proper waste disposal. 
 
 
 
• **Related Government Programs:** 
 
 
• **National Rural Health Mission (NRHM):** Supports the sanitation goals of SBM by improving health outcomes in rural areas. 
 
• **Namami Gange Program:** Works alongside SBM to clean the Ganges river and promote sanitation practices in adjacent regions. 
 
• **Smart Cities Mission:** Integrates SBM goals into urban planning to ensure sustainable waste management and sanitation infrastructure.
